para: list: {items: [...], ordered?: boolean, label?: string}. Canonical items are plain strings or arrays of inline elements. Compatibility forms include a single inline object, {para: inline-content}, and key/value record objects rendered as labelled fields. A bare array at block level is invalid.

table: {columns: [string, ...], rows: [[cell, ...], ...], caption?: string}. Each row has exactly as many cells as columns. A cell is a plain string or an array of inline elements, using the same grammar as a paragraph. Structured links must render as links rather than stringified objects. Numeric values in older notes are display-tolerated but should be written as strings.
bold/strong: string-valued bold emphasis. em/italic: string-valued italic emphasis. All four are registered inline forms in paragraphs, list inline arrays and table cells.

runnable: true enables codeblock.exec (boolean) and codeblock.name (string, unique across the entire document, including nested sections/details). Ordinary renderers display code and never execute it. Execution behaviour belongs to the Notes Browser; see

Write codeblock.lang and codeblock.body. Older language/text aliases are retained only by compatibility renderers that already accepted them; the linter reports them and new producers must use canonical fields. Canonical fields take precedence when both are supplied. No corpus-wide automatic alias rewrite is performed.

Unknown blocks and inline elements are skipped by base consumers; schema validation reports them as unsupported. Malformed known elements are validation errors: validate before rendering rather than rely on renderer-specific recovery. Unknown top-level metadata is allowed by the base format.
bullet_list and writable_note remain application-specific, unregistered blocks. The web viewer's legacy support is not a promise of portable behaviour; use list for portable lists.

Web renderer (notes_web.py), both gdata desktop viewers, shared Envoy JSONHTLRenderer, and its static exporter support section, list, table, bold, image, svg and details. Nested section levels default to 2 at document root (below the document title) and parent effective level + 1, capped at 6; details is transparent to section depth.

Web/static details is browser-native and collapsible. wx.html desktop consumers expose its summary and content expanded; native collapse widgets remain separate UI work. The gdata desktop viewers rasterise SVG and decode raster images. The shared HTML renderer outputs image data URIs for browser display.

codeblock.body:
python3 lint_jsonhtl.py --key README
python3 lint_jsonhtl.py --file document.json --schema jsonhtl_schema.json
python3 lint_jsonhtl.py --all --metadata --links

para: The linter reads the live JSONHTL_SCHEMA by default; --schema accepts an offline copy. It checks nested blocks, aliases, runnable fields/names, table widths, and optionally notes-store metadata and internal hrefs. --links checks against the public key listing: references to private notes require manual classification, and unresolved hrefs are not proof that a note is orphaned.

Any future format change must update spec/registry, schema, linter, web renderer, desktop viewers, shared renderer/exporter, and compatibility tests together. Preserve existing notes; document producer rules and deliberate consumer fallbacks.
